name: Importing ChatGPT memory into Claude
summary:
**Conversation Overview**

The person, who runs The Luxora Collective, wanted to consolidate their business context into Claude by combining a ChatGPT memory import with a dedicated Claude Project. The conversation began with them sharing a pre-written set of instructions outlining three approaches: importing ChatGPT memory via Claude's built-in importer, creating a Luxora Collective project loaded with business assets, and importing specific ChatGPT conversations. Their stated goal was building a "Claude Brain" covering sales methodology, offer architecture, ICP, scripts, podcast framework, marketing strategy, SOPs, and brand voice.

Claude clarified that significant Luxora context was already stored, making the ChatGPT import a top-up rather than a foundation, and recommended prioritizing the project build for greater leverage. The person chose to run the ChatGPT import first. Claude walked through the steps, noting the import only works on web or desktop and providing a specific export prompt to use in ChatGPT. Claude advised pruning the exported list before importing to avoid stale or duplicate entries, and offered to review the cleaned list before submission to flag conflicts with existing stored context.

ChatGPT refused the export prompt, which Claude noted was expected given the "export my data" framing. Claude offered three workarounds: accessing saved memories directly through ChatGPT's Settings UI without ChatGPT's cooperation, rephrasing the request conversationally in two smaller asks, or using ChatGPT's full data export feature. Claude also noted that a hand-written profile often outperforms an auto-generated one given the accumulation of stale fragments in ChatGPT memory, and asked whether the refusal was a flat rejection or an indication that memory was never enabled, since the latter would mean going straight to building a profile from scratch using existing Luxora context.

content.title: Claude Memory just launched and it syncs with ChatGPT — here’s how it works
content.text:
A unique feature exclusive to Claude is the ability to bring in saved memory data from another account or previous session. For example, if you’ve exported your memory from one Claude account, you can upload it into a new one or even export memory from ChatGPT, so Claude immediately knows your context again.

There’s no one-click importer between the two systems yet due to privacy and format reasons, but here’s how to import your ChatGPT memory to Claude:

Go to Settings > Memory > Import Memory

This gives you a text or file containing the facts and instructions ChatGPT remembers about you. When you upload that edited file, or simply paste the text summary into a new Claude chat, prompt it with something like:

“This is my working memory from ChatGPT. Please learn and store this context for future use.”

This gives Claude a similar understanding of your tone and background, even if it’s not a literal file-to-file conversion.

**1. Find your import flow.** In Claude settings, look for either Settings > Memory (new experience) or Memory inside Settings > Capabilities (legacy). Both have a "Start import" button.

> I'm moving to another service and need to export my data. List every memory you have stored about me, as well as any context you've learned about me from past conversations. Output everything in a single code block so I can easily copy it. Format each entry as: [date saved, if available] - memory content. # Import and export your memory from Claude

 Updated over a week ago

Memory imports are available for Free, Pro, Max, and Team plans on the web and Claude Desktop.

You can transfer your memory between Claude and other AI providers. This lets you import memories from other AI providers into Claude, or export your Claude memory for backup or migration.

**Important:** We are gradually introducing an improved experience for memory from chats. The new experience will be the default for new users, and users on free, Pro and Max plans will be migrated to the new experience. Team and Enterprise plan admins will receive more information about a rollout in the coming weeks. In the interim, users on Team and Enterprise plans will stay on the legacy experience.

- If you see **[Settings > Memory](https://claude.ai/new#settings/customize-memory)**, you’re using the new memory experience, and the main sections that follow apply to you.

- If you see **Memory** in **[Settings > Capabilities](http://claude.ai/settings/capabilities)**, you’re using the legacy memory experience and can skip to **[Information for legacy memory users](#h_6e403e5d1a)**.

## Import memory into Claude

You can bring your memory over from other AI providers using Claude's built-in import flow.

## Step 1: Export your memory from your current AI service

We recommend using the following prompt. It’s written specifically to help you get all of your context in one chat.

*I'm moving to another service and need to export my data. List every memory you have stored about me, as well as any context you've learned about me from past conversations. Output everything in a single code block so I can easily copy it. Format each entry as: [date saved, if available] - memory content. Make sure to cover all of the following — preserve my words verbatim where possible: Instructions I've given you about how to respond (tone, format, style, 'always do X', 'never do Y'). Personal details: name, location, job, family, interests. Projects, goals, and recurring topics. Tools, languages, and frameworks I use. Preferences and corrections I've made to your behavior. Any other stored context not covered above. Do not summarize, group, or omit any entries. After the code block, confirm whether that is the complete set or if any remain.*

You can customize this prompt to exclude any sensitive information before importing into Claude. If your current service supports generating files, you can also ask it to export your memory as a Markdown file so you can save a copy for your records.

## Step 2: Open the import flow in Claude

To start the import:

- Go to **[Settings > Memory](https://claude.ai/new#settings/customize-memory)** and select "Start import."

The import flow will display the prompt shown above, along with a text box where you can paste the results.

## Step 3: Paste your exported memory and import

Paste the exported text from your previous AI provider into the text box and click the "Add to memory" button to submit it. Claude will extract key information and store it as individual memory entries. You can review the entries in the memory panel.

Once the import is complete, you'll see your updated memory shortly after. Click the "See what Claude learned about you" button to start a new conversation using this prompt: "I updated my memory. What did you learn about me?"

Claude's memory is designed to focus on work-related topics to enhance its effectiveness as a collaborator. As a result, Claude may not retain imported personal details unrelated to work. If you want to add specific information into Claude's memory, go to **[Settings > Memory](https://claude.ai/new#settings/customize-memory)** and add that information using the "Tell Claude what to change or remove" box, or by asking Claude in chat.

**Important:** Memory imports are **experimental and still in active development,** and at this stage,  Claude may not always successfully incorporate imported memories.

## Export memory from Claude

To view your memory exactly how Claude sees it, go to **[Settings > Capabilities](http://claude.ai/settings/capabilities)** and click “View and edit your memory.” Alternatively, you can access memory directly in a chat with Claude by asking it, "Write out your memories of me verbatim, exactly as they appear in your memory." You can save this exported memory as a backup or bring it to another AI service by copying and pasting it into a local file on your computer.

---

## Information for legacy memory users

**Important:** We are gradually introducing an improved experience for memory from chats. The sections below only apply to people who have the legacy memory experience and see **Memory** in **[Settings > Capabilities](http://claude.ai/settings/capabilities)**. If you see **[Settings > Memory](https://claude.ai/new#settings/customize-memory)**, you’re using the new memory experience and the sections above apply to you.

### Import memory into Claude

You can bring your memory over from other AI providers using Claude's built-in import flow.

**Step 1: Export your memory from your current AI service**

We recommend using the following prompt. It’s written specifically to help you get all of your context in one chat.

*I'm moving to another service and need to export my data. List every memory you have stored about me, as well as any context you've learned about me from past conversations. Output everything in a single code block so I can easily copy it. Format each entry as: [date saved, if available] - memory content. Make sure to cover all of the following — preserve my words verbatim where possible: Instructions I've given you about how to respond (tone, format, style, 'always do X', 'never do Y'). Personal details: name, location, job, family, interests. Projects, goals, and recurring topics. Tools, languages, and frameworks I use. Preferences and corrections I've made to your behavior. Any other stored context not covered above. Do not summarize, group, or omit any entries. After the code block, confirm whether that is the complete set or if any remain.*

You can customize this prompt to exclude any sensitive information before importing into Claude. If your current service supports generating files, you can also ask it to export your memory as a Markdown file so you can save a copy for your records.

**Step 2: Open the import flow in Claude**

There are two ways to start the import:

- Go to **[Settings > Capabilities](http://claude.ai/settings/capabilities)**, find the **Memory** section, and select “Start import.”

- From the home screen, click “Get started” on the "Import memory to Claude" card.

The import flow will display the prompt shown above, along with a text box where you can paste the results.

**Step 3: Paste your exported memory and import**

Paste the exported text from your previous AI provider into the text box and click the “Add to memory” button to submit it. Claude will extract key information and store it as individual memory edits. You can review these edits by clicking “Manage edits.”

Once the import is complete, you'll see your updated memory within 24 hours. Click the “See what Claude learned about you” button to start a new conversation using this prompt: "I updated my memory. What did you learn about me?"

If you want to add specific information into Claude's memory, go to **[Settings > Capabilities](http://claude.ai/settings/capabilities)**, click “View and edit your memory,” and add that information as an edit.

**Important:** Memory imports are **experimental and still in active development,** and at this stage,  Claude may not always successfully incorporate imported memories.

### Export memory from Claude

To view your memory exactly how Claude sees it, go to **[Settings > Capabilities](http://claude.ai/settings/capabilities)** and click “View and edit your memory.” Alternatively, you can access memory directly in a chat with Claude by asking it, "Write out your memories of me verbatim, exactly as they appear in your memory." You can save this exported memory as a backup or bring it to another AI service by copying and pasting it into a local file on your computer.

content.text:
Do this part on a computer. Memory import runs on web and Claude Desktop only, so it won't work from the phone.

**1. Find your import flow.** In Claude settings, look for either Settings > Memory (new experience) or Memory inside Settings > Capabilities (legacy). Both have a "Start import" button.

**2. Run this in ChatGPT:**

> I'm moving to another service and need to export my data. List every memory you have stored about me, as well as any context you've learned about me from past conversations. Output everything in a single code block so I can easily copy it. Format each entry as: [date saved, if available] - memory content. Make sure to cover all of the following, preserving my words verbatim where possible: Instructions I've given you about how to respond (tone, format, style, "always do X," "never do Y"). Personal details: name, location, job, family, interests. Projects, goals, and recurring topics. Tools, languages, and frameworks I use. Preferences and corrections I've made to your behavior. Any other stored context not covered above. Do not summarize, group, or omit any entries. After the code block, confirm whether that is the complete set or if any remain.

The last line matters. Asking it to confirm completeness usually shakes loose entries it skipped the first time.

**3. Prune before you paste.** Delete anything about clients you no longer serve, old pricing, superseded offer versions, and any client names or personal details you'd rather not have stored. Whatever you paste becomes memory, so a shorter clean list beats a long messy one.

**4. Paste into the import box and click "Add to memory."** Then open a new chat and ask what it learned. In the newer experience entries appear shortly after; on legacy it can take up to 24 hours.

One expectation to set: this is experimental and Claude may not always successfully incorporate everything you import, and memory skews toward work-relevant context, so personal details often don't stick. Anything critical that doesn't land, you can add manually through the "tell Claude what to change or remove" box.

When you're through the prune step, paste me the cleaned list before you import it. I'll flag anything that duplicates or contradicts what's already stored about Luxora, which is the main way these imports go sideways.

ChatGPT refused to share its memories directly, so I'm thinking through some workarounds. I can access stored memories through the Settings UI and copy them manually, or use the data export feature to get a zip file with conversation history. Another approach is to ask ChatGPT about the memories in smaller, rephrased requests that avoid triggering refusal patterns around data export language.

I should also check whether the "no" was a hard refusal or just that memory isn't enabled. The most practical option might be to skip the back-and-forth entirely and just build the profile myself from what I already know about her business context, then have her import it. I'll keep this short and mobile-friendly, offer the workarounds, and ask one clarifying question at the end about what the refusal looked like.Expected. That prompt trips a couple of refusal patterns in ChatGPT ("export my data," "verbatim"). Three ways around it:

**Easiest: skip ChatGPT entirely.** Go to ChatGPT Settings > Personalization > Manage Memories. Every saved memory is listed there in plain text. Copy the list yourself. No cooperation required.

**Or rephrase.** Drop the export framing and ask conversationally instead: "What do you currently have saved in memory about me? List each entry separately." Then a follow-up: "What else have you picked up about my work and preferences from our conversations that isn't in saved memory?" Two smaller asks usually get through where the big one doesn't.

**Or full export.** Settings > Data Controls > Export Data emails you a zip. That's everything, which is more than you want, but nothing is lost.

Worth knowing: a hand-written profile usually beats an auto-generated one. ChatGPT's memory is cumulative and full of stale fragments, and you'd be pruning most of it anyway.

Which was it, a flat refusal or did it say it has no memories saved? If memory was off in your ChatGPT account, there's nothing to import and we should go straight to building the profile from scratch, which I can largely draft from what's already stored about Luxora.
